systems.title: Visual Exploration of Big Spatio-Temporal Urban Data: A Study of New York City Taxi Trips
Urban Pulse: Capturing the Rhythm of Cities

nodes.name: Taxi Trip
nodes.description: The data used in our study was provided by Taxi and Limousine Commission of New York City and contains information about all medallion taxi trips in 2009, 2011, and 2012.
inputs: Raw CSV files from NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission
outputs: Structured dataset of taxi trips with attributes like trip id, taxi id, pickup/dropoff locations and times, distance, fare amount, tip amount, and toll amount
nodes.citation: Data and Design Requirements section: The data used in our study was provided by Taxi and Limousine Commission of New York City and contains information about all medallion taxi trips in 2009, 2011, and 2012.

nodes.name: Spatiotemporal Index
nodes.description: We have built a specialized index based on k-d trees to support spatio-temporal queries at interactive rates.
outputs: Indexed data structure supporting spatio-temporal constraints
nodes.citation: The TaxiVis System section: We have built a specialized index based on k-d trees to support spatio-temporal queries at interactive rates.

nodes.name: Visual Query Engine
nodes.description: Users formulate queries visually, by interacting with maps and other visual representations. Internally, a textual query is generated which is then evaluated by the storage manager.
outputs: Query result set (subset of taxi trips)
nodes.citation: The TaxiVis System section: Users formulate queries visually, by interacting with maps and other visual representations. Internally, a textual query is generated which is then evaluated by the storage manager.

nodes.name: Map 2D
nodes.description: Maps serve different purposes in our system. They provide a canvas for displaying query results, for users to specify spatial constraints and compose/refine queries.
outputs: Interactive 2D map view with pickups, drop-offs, directional constraints
nodes.citation: User Interface Components section: Maps serve different purposes in our system. They provide a canvas for displaying query results, for users to specify spatial constraints and compose/refine queries.

nodes.name: Overlay (Heatmap)
nodes.description: Our system supports density summary visualizations or heat maps that can be used to show the distribution of pickups and/or dropoffs in an area.
outputs: Heatmap overlay on 2D map
nodes.citation: Query Result Visualization section: Our system supports density summary visualizations or heat maps that can be used to show the distribution of pickups and/or dropoffs in an area.

nodes.name: Grid Map
nodes.description: A grid map is a set of cells where their geometries and visual representations can be customized by the users.
outputs: Grid-based map visualization by region (e.g., neighborhoods, zip codes)
nodes.citation: Query Result Visualization section: A grid map is a set of cells where their geometries and visual representations can be customized by the users.

nodes.name: Time Series
nodes.description: The information associated with the results of a query can be visualized using different representations within the data summary view, such as time series.
outputs: Time series plots of taxi trips over time
nodes.citation: User Interface Components section: The information associated with the results of a query can be visualized using different representations within the data summary view, such as time series.

nodes.name: Histogram
nodes.description: The attribute selection view shows histograms that summarize the attribute values for the trips in the result set of the query.
outputs: Histograms of attribute distributions (e.g., fare, tip amount)
nodes.citation: Visual Query Specification section: The attribute selection view shows histograms that summarize the attribute values for the trips in the result set of the query.

nodes.name: Scatter Plot
nodes.description: Scatter plots are used to examine the duration of trips to the airports at different times of the day.
outputs: Scatter plots showing relationships between attributes (e.g., trip duration vs. time of day)
nodes.citation: Exploring Query Results section: Scatter plots are used to examine the duration of trips to the airports at different times of the day.

nodes.name: Area Selection
nodes.description: Spatial constraints are specified by polygons and arrows on the map view. These are created either by brushing or by selecting predefined polygons corresponding to NYC's neighborhoods, zip codes, and boroughs.
outputs: Spatial query constraints
nodes.citation: Visual Query Specification section: Spatial constraints are specified by polygons and arrows on the map view. These are created either by brushing or by selecting predefined polygons corresponding to NYC's neighborhoods, zip codes, and boroughs.

nodes.name: Temporal Selection
nodes.description: Temporal constraints are specified using the time selection widgets. In the Regular Selection widget, the user defines an atomic temporal constraint by assigning the values of the start time and end time fields.
outputs: Temporal query constraints
nodes.citation: Visual Query Specification section: Temporal constraints are specified using the time selection widgets. In the Regular Selection widget, the user defines an atomic temporal constraint by assigning the values of the start time and end time fields.

nodes.name: Attribute Filter
nodes.description: Attribute constraints are defined through the attribute selection view, which shows histograms that summarize the attribute values for the trips in the result set of the query.
outputs: Attribute query constraints
nodes.citation: Visual Query Specification section: Attribute constraints are defined through the attribute selection view, which shows histograms that summarize the attribute values for the trips in the result set of the query.

nodes.name: Spatiotemporal Images Dataset
nodes.description: Loads Flickr data including image metadata (timestamps and geolocations) to capture the dynamic events of the city
inputs: Raw Flickr data (images with spatiotemporal metadata)
outputs: Structured spatiotemporal dataset for density function computation
nodes.citation: All the data sets used in this paper are composed of a set of data points over space and time. (Introduction / Section 3)

nodes.name: 2D Features
nodes.description: Loads a planar mesh representing the city's spatial domain
outputs: Triangulated 2D mesh representing the city's spatial features
nodes.citation: Mesh representation of a city. Given a city, the mesh corresponding to it represents the bounding box... (Mesh Representation section)

nodes.name: Prominent Density Feature Identification
nodes.description: Aggregates high-persistence topological features to identify prominent locations based on high density focusing on the computed density rather than using the author's pulse terminology
outputs: Identified prominent density features (i.e. locations with high density)
nodes.citation: a prominent location is a high persistent maximum of a function... (Section 4.1)

nodes.name: Significant Density Profile
nodes.description: Derives a binary (0/1) sequence indicating, for each time step, whether a significant (high-persistence) maximum is present at the location
inputs: Density functions at the identified locations
outputs: Binary sequence (significant density profile) per location
nodes.citation: Significant Beats Bs: This is a 0/1 sequence indicating the absence/presence of a high persistent maximum... (Section 4.2 adapted)

nodes.name: Maxima Density Profile
nodes.description: Computes a binary sequence that records, for each time step, whether any local maximum is present at the location, regardless of persistence
inputs: Density functions at the identified locations
outputs: Binary sequence (maxima density profile) per location
nodes.citation: Maxima Beats Bm: This is a 0/1 sequence indicating the absence/presence of a maximum at the location... (Section 4.2 adapted)

nodes.name: Density Function Profile
nodes.description: Generates a continuous time series capturing the variation of the density function value at the location, representing the magnitude of density over time
inputs: Density functions at the identified locations
outputs: Continuous time series (density function profile) per location
nodes.citation: Function Beats Bf: This is a time series showing the variation of the scalar function at that location... (Section 4.2 adapted)

nodes.name: High-dimensional Density Feature Vector
nodes.description: Constructs a high-dimensional feature vector from the three density profiles (significant, maxima, and function) and computes an L2-norm rank to quantify overall density intensity
inputs: Combined density profiles across all resolutions
outputs: Numeric rank score derived from the L2 norm of the density feature vector
nodes.citation: For a given pulse P, its rank is computed as the L2 norm of its corresponding feature vector... (Section 4.3 adapted as density feature vector)

nodes.name: Euclidean Distance of Density Feature Vectors
nodes.description: Calculates similarity between locations by computing the Euclidean distance between their high-dimensional density feature vectors
outputs: Similarity measure (L2 norm distance) between density features
nodes.citation: Pulse Similarity is defined as the L2 norm of the similarity vector computed from the differences between beats... (Section 4.3 adapted to density feature vectors)

nodes.name: Map 2D
nodes.description: Renders a 2D map that displays the spatial regions corresponding to the identified density feature locations, optionally overlaying a heatmap of the computed density values
outputs: 2D map visualization
nodes.citation: Map widget. The map view component consists of one or more map widgets... (Section 6 adapted as Map 2D)

nodes.name: Overlay (Heatmap)
nodes.description: Renders a heatmap overlay on the 2D map to visually represent the computed density values across different spatial locations
outputs: 2D heatmap overlay integrated with the map view
nodes.citation: optional heat map overlay of the density function. (Section 6 adapted)

nodes.name: Scatter Plot
nodes.description: Visualizes density ranking data using a scatter plot, enabling comparison of density features across different temporal resolutions
outputs: Scatter plot showing density feature rankings
nodes.citation: Linked scatter plots. The default mode of the Pulse Monitor consists of three linked scatter plots... (Section 6 adapted as Scatter Plot)

nodes.name: Line Chart
nodes.description: Displays the density function profile as a line chart plotting time steps against density values to illustrate temporal variations at a location
outputs: Line chart visualizing temporal variation of density magnitudes
nodes.citation: The pulse beat viewer visualizes function beats as a line plot... (Section 6.1 adapted as Line Chart)

nodes.name: Plot Brush
nodes.description: Enables users to filter density feature locations by brushing over the scatter plot, linking the selection to updates across all visualizations
inputs: User brush input on the scatter plot
outputs: Filtered density feature locations highlighted in both scatter plot and map view
nodes.citation: Pulse filtering and exploration. Users can select pulses of interest by brushing one of the scatter plots... (Section 6.2 adapted as Scatter Plot Brush)

nodes.name: Area Selection
nodes.description: Allows users to directly select a geographic area on the map to filter and display density feature locations within that area
outputs: Density features within the selected area are highlighted/filtered
nodes.citation: The map view component provides spatial context for pulses... (Section 6 inferred for Area Selection)

nodes.name: Pulse Selection
nodes.description: Queries for similar pulses based on similarity measures and user input returns a ranked list of similar pulses for visualization
outputs: Ranked list of similar pulses to update visualizations (e.g., scatter plot)
nodes.citation: ...similarity and vice versa. For example, consider the pulse corresponding to Alcatraz Island in San Francisco (SF) shown in Fig. 5... Section 4.3
